## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Pārāpariyattheragāthā* (Thag 16.10) is a verse text belonging to the *Theragāthā* in the *Khuddakanikāya* of the Pali Tipiṭaka [SuttaCentral]. It forms the tenth piece in the sixteenth chapter (*Soḷasakanipāta*) of the collection [SuttaCentral]. In secondary scholarship, Walpola Rahula mentions the *Pārāpariyattheragāthā* in passing when discussing how the Buddha refrained from laying down disciplinary rules until occasions specifically required them, drawing a comparison with the Buddha's explanation to Bhaddāli [Rahula 1978]. The text has received nine translations across eight languages, including an English translation by Bhikkhu Sujato [SuttaCentral].

No curated parallels in other early Buddhist collections are recorded by SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral]. Computerized analysis via DharmaNexus demonstrates widespread text reuse within Pali literature, detecting 20 shared segments (comprising over 5,300 characters) between the verses of Thag 16.10 and the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* (*Dutiyo bhāgo*), with the most extensive match covering segments 1.4–15.3 [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language matches, DharmaNexus detects low-plausibility automatic alignments (score 20) with passages in the Tibetan Kangyur translation of the *Ārya-caturdārakasamādhi-nāma-mahāyāna-sūtra* (D0136 / H0137) at segments 27.4–28.3, though these reflect shared phraseology rather than direct parallels [DharmaNexus].
